name: Wimberley Market Days
desc: One of the Hill Country's oldest open-air markets, held the first Saturday of each month March–December at Lions Field. Booths are $125 ($75 in summer) and assigned by seniority; new vendors join a rolling waitlist by email.
notes: First-Saturday open-air market running March through December. Booth spaces are assigned by seniority, with a rolling waitlist for new vendors. Approval is rolling via email (leasing@wimberleymarketday.com), not a fixed application deadline; booths are typically rented the week before each market day. Pricing is tiered: $125 is the standard monthly rate, with a discounted $75 summer-season rate (roughly Jun-Aug) and a separate $100 Friday-evening rate — this listing's Sept 5 date falls outside the summer window, so $125 is the applicable figure.

name: Fredericksburg Trade Days
desc: Three-day market the third weekend of every month across covered barns and open lots. Outdoor lots run $75–$135 and indoor barn spaces $150–$273; book by phone, no jury.
notes: Three-day Hill Country market held the third weekend of each month across covered barns and open field lots. Pricing varies by space: $75-$135 for outdoor lots, $150-$273 for indoor barn spaces (10x14 to 15x14). No published application deadline or jury process; contact 210-846-4094 to book.

name: Bayou City Art Festival Downtown
desc: Houston's flagship juried fine art festival, spring edition, in Sam Houston Park and along Allen Parkway. Blind scoring by a 5–7 juror panel; $50 jury fee, notifications Dec 14.
notes:
Juried fine art festival drawing a national applicant pool across 19 media categories. Panel review with blind scoring. This is the Memorial Park edition (Fri-Sun); booth fees range $525-$1775 by category/size plus a separate $50 non-refundable jury fee. Accepted artists notified by Jul 6. Public admission is $18 early-bird/$20 regular per day (kids 6-12 $5, 5 and under free), or $30 for a weekend pass.

2026-10-28 roll-forward: Memorial Park Oct 2026 edition ended; listing now tracks Downtown spring 2027 (Apr 3-4) per OpenCall listing (deadline Nov 29, 2026, $50 app fee, notify Dec 14). Spring festival moved downtown per official apply page (apps opened Sep 1, 2026). Booth fee $625-$1,875 per VendorsMap; not yet confirmed on official site. Admission for downtown edition not published.

name: Comicpalooza
desc: Houston's big multi-genre pop culture convention at the George R. Brown, with an Artist Alley that sells out in price tiers. 2027 dates are expected over Memorial Day weekend; exhibitor pricing isn't posted yet.
notes:
Multi-genre pop culture convention with a dedicated Artist Alley. Tables sell out in tiers; early registration opens to prior-year vendors. UNVERIFIED: 2027 exhibitor applications aren't open yet (interest form only as of Aug 2026) — no official 2027 dates, pricing, or deadline published. Current start/end/deadline/fee below are unconfirmed placeholders. Public admission ($68 single-day, ~$119 weekend pass) is reference pricing carried over from the completed May 2026 event via secondary media coverage — the official site no longer publishes 2026 prices and hasn't posted 2027 numbers yet.

2026-10-28: replaced Jan 2027 placeholder with May 28-30, 2027 (VendorsMap 'expected'); treated as rolling (tables sell in tiers until gone). Fee/admission set to null until 2027 pricing is published.

name: Armadillo Christmas Bazaar
desc: Austin's ten-day juried holiday art market with live music at Palmer Events Center; best for vendors with deep inventory and help staffing. Booths run about $1,500–$5,000+; applications are rolling, with Jan–Mar submissions reviewed first.
notes: Ten-day juried holiday art market with live music. Long-run format favors vendors with deep inventory and staffing help. Booth fees run ~$1,500-$5,000+ by size (avg ~$2,000) plus a $25 application fee. Applications are accepted year-round on a rolling basis; Jan-Mar submissions get priority, with primary review Mar-Aug. Returning artists get priority over new applicants in popular categories. Public admission is $12 (+fees, ~$14 total) per day, or $60 for a season pass; kids 12 and under free.

name: First Monday Trade Days
desc: One of the country's largest flea markets, spread over hundreds of acres for the four days before the first Monday of each month. Pavilions set their own rates, so call the City of Canton office (903-567-6556) for space pricing.
notes: One of the largest recurring open-air markets in the country, spanning several hundred acres over four days each month. UNVERIFIED: the grounds are split across many independently-operated pavilions, each with its own booth pricing and contact — there is no single official fee. Call the City of Canton First Monday office at 903-567-6556 for a specific venue's rate.

name: Cottonwood Art Festival
desc: Richardson's twice-yearly juried fine art festival under the trees of Cottonwood Park, with about 190 artist spots in spring. $500 single booth plus $35 jury fee; free admission and parking.
notes:
Twice-yearly juried fine art festival in a shaded park setting. Jury reviews three work images plus one booth shot. $500 covers a single booth; a double booth is $1,000 (limited) and electricity is a $100 add-on. A separate $35 non-refundable jury/application fee is paid per entry via ZAPPlication.

2026-10-28 roll-forward: Oct 2026 edition ended; Spring 2027 is May 1-2, apply by Dec 8, 2026, $500 single / $1,000 double, +$100 electricity, $35 jury fee, ~190 open spots (official artist-resources page).

name: Blue Genie Art Bazaar
desc: Consignment-style holiday bazaar in East Austin: no booth fee or staffing; the shop takes a percentage of sales instead. The 2026 run is Nov 13–Dec 24, and the next submission window typically opens in May ($45 application fee).
notes: Consignment-model holiday bazaar. No booth fee or staffing requirement; the venue takes a percentage of sales instead, plus a $45 non-refundable application fee. The Yelp "Temporarily Closed" status is normal seasonal downtime, not a shutdown — the storefront is a holiday-only operation that reopens each November for the season, running Nov 13-Dec 24, 2026 (corrected from an earlier Nov 27 start). Public admission is believed free (multiple secondary sources agree; the official FAQ page returned a 404 during verification, so treat as likely rather than confirmed). The 2026 submission window ran May 1-Jul 31 and has already closed as of this listing's last check — this is now a "watch for next May's window" reference for vendors, not a currently-open call; the shop itself is still on for its Nov-Dec 2026 run.

name: Anime Matsuri
desc: Houston anime and Japanese culture convention with a large Artist Alley and separate dealer hall; 2027 runs Jul 22–25 at the George R. Brown. Table prices step up Dec 1, Mar 1, Apr 1 and Jun 1, so apply early for the lowest tier.
notes: Anime and Japanese culture convention with a large artist alley and separate dealer hall. Table assignment by registration order. Corrected from a stale March placeholder — Anime Matsuri actually runs in July; the 2026 edition (Jul 23-26) is confirmed and uncancelled, and 2027 is set for Jul 22-25 (per Eventbrite, though organizers note dates may shift). Applications open Sept 8 with price tiers increasing Dec 1/Mar 1/Apr 1/Jun 1 - exact table price not published outside the application form, so the $380 figure and Dec 1 "deadline" (first price-increase date) are best-effort estimates. Public admission tiers are $65 Fri/$70 Sat/$45 Sun from the official badge page, but tied to the just-completed 2026 dates and carried as reference pricing since 2027 isn't priced yet.

name: Main Street Fort Worth Arts Festival
desc: Four-day juried street festival with some of the heaviest foot traffic in Texas: about 220 artists chosen from nearly 1,000 applicants. 10x10 booths are $995 ($1,145 corner) on pavement, so bring weights.
notes: Four-day juried street festival with very high foot traffic. Booths are on pavement; weights required in place of stakes. Standard 10x10 booth is $995 (corner $1,145), plus a separate $40 non-refundable application fee. 220 artists are jury-selected from nearly 1,000 applicants (2026 cycle figure).

name: Emerald City Comic Con
desc: Seattle's major comics convention, listed for Texas artists who tour nationally. Artist Alley is curated by portfolio review; $430 gets a 6' table and two badges.
notes: Artist Alley is curated via portfolio review, not a lottery or first-come order. Accepted artists get a 6' table plus 2 badges for $430. Corrected: 2027 applications are open, not closed — the real deadline is Oct 29, 2026 at 5:00pm PT, with notifications going out Nov 13, 2026 (an earlier version of this listing incorrectly showed a Jan 16, 2027 deadline and claimed applications had already closed with only a waitlist available). Public admission is $84 Saturday single-day (tax/fees included), $64.05 Fri/Sun, $27.30 Thursday preview — confirmed on the official 2027 ticket page.

name: Round Top Antiques Fair
desc: Two-and-a-half-week antiques destination spread across 48+ independently run show fields along Highway 237. Space is leased directly from each field (Marburger Farm, Zapp Hall, Big Red Barn and others), so rates and applications vary.
notes: Roughly two-and-a-half-week destination market spread across 48+ independent show fields (not nine days as previously listed). Early fields like Bar W Field, Henkel Square, and The Marketplace Warrenton open Oct 15; most of the 48+ venues run the official Oct 17-31 window. Space is leased directly from individual field operators (e.g. Zapp Hall, Excess Fields, Marburger Farm, Big Red Barn) - pricing and application process vary by field and remain unconfirmed here; the $900 fee is an unverified placeholder. Public admission is similarly fragmented across the 48+ fields — most are free to browse, but the flagship "Original Round Top Antiques Fair" field charges its own $10 general/$25 VIP admission, so no single admission price applies to the market as a whole.

name: Texas Renaissance Festival
desc: Texas's largest Renaissance festival, running eight themed weekends Oct 10–Nov 29 plus Thanksgiving Friday. Shops must be period-appropriate; new-vendor applications ($50 fee) are accepted on a rolling basis.
notes: Eight-weekend seasonal festival requiring period-appropriate merchandise and shop presentation. Multi-season vendors get renewal priority. Corrected start date: the official site confirms the 2026 season runs Oct 10-Nov 29 plus Thanksgiving Friday (the previously listed Oct 3 start was wrong — Oct 3 isn't part of the season). Confirmed: the vendor application itself carries a $50 non-refundable fee. The $1,400 figure here is presumed to be the actual shop/booth lease, but I could not confirm that number from the source PDF (binary-encoded, didn't extract cleanly) — needs a second look. No official application deadline is published — the site currently states it's still accepting new-vendor applications on a rolling basis, so the date shown is an estimated planning buffer, not a hard cutoff. Public admission is NOT free and has no single flat price — the official site confirms dynamic per-weekend pricing from roughly $16-27 (early/off-peak weekends like Oktoberfest) up to $28-46+ (peak weekends like Pirate Adventure, Halloween, Highland Fling), advance vs. gate. The $28 stored here is a typical non-peak gate-day figure, not an official constant.

name: Dallas Fan Expo
desc: Dallas's largest pop culture convention moves to June in 2027 at the Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center. Artist Alley tables are $505 standard or $1,110 premium end-cap; applications are reviewed and tables sell until gone.
notes:
Large pop culture convention with tiered artist alley pricing by table location and corner access. Corrected from a placeholder May 2027 date - the confirmed, upcoming edition is Sep 11-13, 2026 at the Kay Bailey Hutchison Convention Center (2027 dates aren't announced yet). Standard 6x5 table is $480; premium 5x12 end-cap is $1,060. No fixed application deadline is published - tables sell until they run out, so this date is an estimated planning buffer, not an official cutoff. Public single-day admission is $58 Saturday/$48 Sunday/$33 Friday per the official ticketing partner's live checkout page (base price before service fee) — confirmed as current pricing, though the site notes "advanced pricing" ends Aug 27, 2026 and may step up to a higher tier before the show.

2026-10-28 roll-forward: Sep 2026 edition ended. Official artist-alley page: 2027 is Jun 11-13, 'Apply for 2027' open, Standard 6x5 $505, Premium 5x12 $1,110. No deadline published (rolling). 2027 admission not yet published.

name: Nutcracker Market
desc: Houston Ballet's massive juried holiday market at NRG Center, drawing 100,000+ shoppers over four days. Booths run roughly $1,800–$4,800 by size, plus an 11% commission on sales.
notes:
Massive juried holiday shopping market fundraising for Houston Ballet, drawing over 100,000 shoppers across a preview party plus four show days at NRG Center. Unlike a flat booth-fee model, Houston Ballet also takes an 11% commission on merchant sales on top of space cost, and charges a separate non-refundable $25 application fee. Exact booth pricing tiers weren't accessible (pricing page blocked automated access), so the $2,500 fee here is a rough placeholder based on comparable high-traffic juried holiday markets, not a confirmed price - confirm real pricing and the application deadline directly before applying. Public admission is $20/day general, or $60 for a 4-day early-bird pass; kids 2 and under free.

2026-10-28: fee updated from $2,500 placeholder to $1,800 low end of $1,800-$4,800 range listed on VendorsMap (plus 11% commission).

name: Boerne Market Days
desc: Hill Country market on Boerne's historic Main Plaza the second weekend of every month, plus extra holiday markets in November and December. Vendors reapply monthly and pay by the 1st of the prior month; contact the organizer for booth pricing.
notes: Recurring Hill Country market on Boerne's historic Main Plaza, held the second weekend of every month, plus three bonus special-event dates not reflected in this listing's auto-computed schedule: a November Holiday Gift Market and two separate December markets (a Christmas Market and a Cowboy Christmas Market) — the organizer's own site cites these three extra dates in its attendance figures. Vendors reapply each month they want to participate. Booth fees must be paid by the 1st of the month before the show and are non-refundable, but the actual dollar amount isn't published online - the $40 here is a rough estimate based on comparable small-town Hill Country markets, not a confirmed price. Contact davidquerbach@eventsoffmain.com or (210) 844-8193 to confirm current pricing and attendance before applying. Public admission is inferred free — the official page lists public market hours with no fee mentioned, but there's no explicit "free" statement either.

name: Art & Beer Night Market Austin
desc: Evening market at The Brewtorium pairing 70+ Austin artists and makers with craft beer. Held the second Saturday of November in recent years; watch @artandbeeraustin for the 2026 call and booth pricing.
notes: Annual evening market at The Brewtorium pairing 70+ local artists/makers with craft beer and food. Confirmed to have run in both 2024 (Nov 9) and 2025 (Nov 8) — both landed on the 2nd Saturday of November, which is the pattern this listing's date is computed from, but the 2026 edition hasn't been officially announced yet, so treat the date as inferred, not confirmed. Booth fee, public admission price, and application deadline are all unconfirmed — no organizer page publishes dollar figures; the $75 fee shown is a rough estimate based on comparable small Austin maker markets. Outdoor/brewery-grounds setting is inferred from the venue, not explicitly stated. Watch the organizer's Instagram (@artandbeeraustin) for the official 2026 announcement before applying.

name: Fiesta Arts Fair
org: UT San Antonio (Southwest School of Art)
desc: Nationally ranked juried fine art and craft fair on the historic Southwest School of Art campus during Fiesta San Antonio, drawing artists from about 30 states. Applications close Nov 1 via ZAPPlication; show dates follow its usual mid-April slot.
notes:
Nationally-ranked juried fine art & craft fair (Top 50, Art Fair SourceBook) held on UTSA's historic Southwest campus as part of Fiesta San Antonio, drawing 100-120+ artists from ~30 states. The Nov 1, 2026 application deadline is real and actionable — applications for the next edition just opened via ZAPPlication — but the show's own 2027 dates aren't announced yet; the Apr 17-18, 2027 shown here is an estimated placeholder following the fair's usual mid-to-late-April slot. Booth fee ($350+) is a stale figure from a 2017-18 secondary source, not confirmed current pricing. The separate ZAPPlication jury/application fee is confirmed current: $25 early-bird (until 9/8/2026), $30 standard, $35 late (after 11/2/2026). Public admission ($16 for a 2-day ticket) is confirmed for the just-completed April 2026 edition. Attendance is a rough midpoint of conflicting secondary estimates (8,000-12,000).

2026-10-28: fee updated from stale $350 to $425 (low end of $425-$650 10x10 range on VendorsMap).

name: Old Gruene Market Days
desc: Juried monthly artisan market of about 100 vendors in the Gruene Historic District, the third full weekend of each month February–November plus early December. Free admission; contact the Gruene Merchants Association for booth pricing.
notes: Long-running monthly artisan market (~100 vendors) in the Gruene Historic District selling handmade crafts and Texas-made packaged foods, with free live entertainment. Runs the 3rd full weekend of the month, February through November, plus a bonus 1st-weekend-of-December date not reflected in this listing's auto-computed schedule (same modeling limitation as Boerne's extra December date — see README). It is juried, so it's not a walk-on market, but no application deadline is published anywhere the organizer's site would confirm (site blocked automated access) — shown as rolling until confirmed; contact the Gruene Merchants Association directly. Booth fee ($60) is an estimate based on comparable small monthly Hill Country markets, not an organizer-published figure. Admission and parking are confirmed free. Attendance (~4,000/weekend) is a secondary-source estimate, not an official organizer figure.

name: Art in the Square
desc: Volunteer-run juried fine art festival at Southlake Town Square benefiting Tarrant County charities, with 150+ artists. $550 single booth, plus a $300 Emerging Artist tier for developing DFW artists; free admission.
notes: Long-running (26+ years) juried fine art festival at Southlake Town Square, run entirely by volunteers of the Southlake Women's Club to benefit Tarrant County charities, drawing 150+ artists and repeatedly ranked #1 by Art Fair SourceBook. Single booth (10'x10') is $550, double is $1,050, and there's a distinctive $300 Emerging Artist tier for developing DFW-area artists — plus a separate $40 non-refundable application fee. Public admission is confirmed free. Attendance is reported as "tens of thousands" across organizer and third-party sources, but no precise official total is published — the 40,000 shown is an order-of-magnitude estimate, not a hard count.

name: Celebration of the Arts
desc: The Permian Basin's long-running indoor fine art and fine craft show at the Bush Convention Center, with cash jury awards. 2027 dates and booth fee aren't announced yet; dates shown follow its usual mid-May slot.
notes: Self-described cornerstone fine art & fine craft event of the Permian Basin, now in its 42nd+ year, held fully indoors (rain-or-shine, air-conditioned) at the Bush Convention Center with 40+ regional/out-of-state artists across painting, fiber, photography, jewelry, wood, and glass, plus cash jury awards. The just-completed 43rd edition's booth fee was never published beyond a $25 non-refundable ZAPPlication application fee — the $450 shown is a rough estimate based on comparably-sized indoor Texas art fairs, not an organizer-confirmed price. 2027 show dates aren't announced yet (next cycle typically opens in December); the May 14-16 window shown is an estimated placeholder following the fair's usual mid-May slot. Saturday/Sunday admission is confirmed free (a separate ticketed Friday preview party is $80-85, not general admission). Attendance is unconfirmed — no official total is published; 5,000 is a conservative estimate for a regional indoor fair of this size.

name: Galveston Craft Show
desc: Juried, handmade-only indoor craft show moving to the Moody Gardens Convention Center for 2027, sharing a ticket with the Corvette/Chevy Expo. 10x10 booths are $125 ($155 corner); applications are open now.
notes:
Juried, handmade-only indoor craft show relocating for 2027 to the Moody Gardens Hotel and Convention Center ("The Founding Year at Moody Gardens"), still run alongside the Corvette/Chevy Expo on one shared ticket. Pricing changed with the venue move: a standard 10x10 booth is now $125 (corner booths, limited availability, are $155) — no longer bundled with admission passes as in prior years at the old Convention Center venue. Vendor applications open Aug 1, 2026 and are juried (curated for product quality/category balance); no fixed application deadline is published, so the date shown here is an estimated planning buffer, not an official cutoff. Public admission is $18 one-day advance / $20 at door, $30-35 for a weekend pass; free for kids 12 and under. Attendance is an estimate carried from the prior venue — unconfirmed for the new location.

2026-10-28: estimated Jan 15 deadline replaced with rolling (organizer publishes no fixed cutoff).

name: ArtWalk Alpine
desc: West Texas's longest-running art festival fills downtown Alpine's sidewalks and studios Nov 20–21, with two music stages and food trucks. Non-juried and free to attend; request the PDF application for booth pricing.
notes: Billed as the longest-running art festival in West Texas, now in its 33rd year — murals, sculpture, photography, and painting fill downtown Alpine's sidewalks and studios over the weekend, alongside two music stages and food trucks. Free to attend and explicitly non-juried, with ~26 exhibitors historically. Booth fee is genuinely not published anywhere online (only a downloadable PDF application is offered) — the $65 shown is a rough estimate based on comparable small non-juried outdoor art walks, not an organizer-confirmed price; request the application directly to learn the real cost. Nov 20-21 dates are confirmed directly on the official site (a secondary source's Nov 20-22 listing does not match and appears to be wrong). Fills the far West Texas / Big Bend region gap.

name: Abilene Holiday Market
desc: Juried one-day holiday gift market at the Mesquite Event Center in downtown Abilene, with 50+ handmade and specialty vendors. Booths from $75 (5x10) to $300 (10x20), plus a $10 application fee.
notes: Juried, single-day indoor holiday gift market at the Mesquite Event Center in downtown Abilene, with 50+ vendors selling handmade and unique goods — fills the Big Country/West-Central Texas region gap. Tiered booth pricing: 5x10 $75, 10x10 $150, 10x15 $200, 10x20 $300, edible vendors (5x8) $50, plus a $10 non-refundable application fee (photos required); organizers explicitly select for handmade/unique quality and event fit. Public admission is $5 general, $3 with student/teacher/military ID, free for kids 11 and under. All core figures — fee tiers, admission, ~1,800 average attendance — are confirmed directly from the organizer's page.

name: Mission Marquee Farmers & Artisans Market
desc: Farmers and artisans market at Mission Marquee Plaza near the Mission Reach, the 1st and 3rd Saturdays March–November. No vendor fee; goods must be handmade, and the plaza curates the vendor mix.
notes: Recurring artisan/farmers market at Mission Marquee Plaza near San Antonio's Mission Reach (Mar-Nov). CONFIRMED: no vendor fee is charged ("No vendor fees will apply" per the official page) - genuinely rare for this directory. Application is via an online Smartsheet form with no fixed deadline; acceptance isn't guaranteed and the plaza reserves discretion over vendor mix, so treated as non-juried/discretionary rather than a formal panel jury. Artisan goods must be handmade - no mass-produced items. Runs BOTH the 1st and 3rd Saturday of each month; this listing's auto-computed schedule follows the 3rd Saturday only (same modeling limitation as Boerne/Gruene's bonus dates - see README), so a 1st-Saturday date each month isn't reflected here. Public admission and attendance are unconfirmed - inferred free (no fee mentioned for visitors) and estimated at a modest 1,500/market day for a single mission-plaza market, not an official figure.

name: Frisco Maker Faire
desc: Free, grant-funded maker showcase at the Frisco Discovery Center, with no fee for makers or visitors. Open to any kind of maker; the 2027 date isn't announced yet, so dates shown follow last year's.
notes: Free, all-ages maker showcase at the Frisco Discovery Center / Sci-Tech Discovery Center, grant-funded so there is genuinely no fee for makers or attendees. The 2026 edition ran Jan 31, 2026 (regular registration closed Dec 15, 2025, late registration to Jan 5, 2026) - that date has already passed as of this listing's verification, so the Jan 30, 2027 date and Dec 15, 2026 deadline shown here are estimated based on the prior year's pattern, not yet officially announced. Open to any "maker" - digital, physical, arts, or music - with December applicants getting priority placement (not a formal jury). Indoor, with overflow to the adjacent Sci-Tech museum galleries. Attendance is unconfirmed - no official figure published; 3,000 is a rough estimate for a single-day free family STEM/maker event of this scale.

name: Frisco Holiday Gift Market
desc: Single-evening city holiday market at Simpson Plaza with Santa photos and the tree lighting. Each booth includes a tent, lighting, table, chairs and power; applications close Nov 1 or when full.
notes: Single-evening city-run holiday market at Simpson Plaza (3-7:30pm) paired with Santa photos, carriage rides, and a tree-lighting ceremony. CONFIRMED: applications close Nov 1, 2026 (or earlier if booths fill), reviewed in order received starting Sep 1; the vendor committee has discretion over quality/fit rather than running a formal blind jury. Each booth includes a 10'x10' tent with lighting, one 6' table, two chairs, a 4-outlet power box, and two parking passes - an unusually full amenity bundle for the fee. UNVERIFIED: exact booth dollar cost isn't published on the official page - the $100 shown is an estimate based on comparably-bundled city-run holiday markets, not a confirmed price; confirm directly via friscotexas.gov before applying. Admission is inferred free (standard for this kind of civic plaza holiday event; not explicitly stated). Attendance is unconfirmed - 5,000 is a rough single-evening estimate.

name: Round Rock Market Days
desc: Monthly artisan fair on Prete Main Street Plaza the first Saturday of each month March–December, with about 120 exhibitors and live music. $85 artisan / $100 business booths, first come, first served.
notes: Recurring monthly artisan/vendor fair at Prete Main Street Plaza in Downtown Round Rock, first Saturday of the month March-December. Corrected: an earlier version of this listing claimed October shifts to the 2nd Saturday - that was checked against the organizer's own schedule and found to be false (the one documented exception is July, not October). ~120 exhibitors, free admission and parking, live music. CONFIRMED booth fee tiers: $85 Artisan Fee / $100 Business Fee. Spaces are first-come-first-served rather than formally juried. No fixed application deadline is published; the date shown is an estimated planning buffer. Attendance is unconfirmed - 6,000 is a rough estimate for a well-attended monthly downtown market of this size, not an official figure.

name: Red Poppy Festival
desc: Georgetown's flagship festival: three days on the historic square with 100–150+ handmade-only artisans and about 75,000 visitors. $400 for a 10x10; 2027 is set for Apr 23–25, and the deadline shown follows last year's.
notes: Georgetown's flagship annual festival (27th edition in 2026), three days on the historic downtown square with live music and 100-150+ artisan vendors selling handmade-only work. Selection is via photo/portfolio review with a handmade-only certification requirement (not a blind panel jury, but not open walk-on either). The Jan 8, 2027 deadline shown is an estimate extrapolated from the prior cycle's Jan 9, 2026 deadline - the 2027 application window wasn't open yet as of this listing's verification. Admission is confirmed free. Attendance (~75,000 over the weekend) is confirmed via the city's special events coordinator.

name: Spring Market in the Vines
desc: Small one-day outdoor market at 3 Texans Winery with wine tasting and live music. $70 per 10x10, paid by the Thursday before; the 2027 date follows last year's pattern.

Only one market day per year has been publicly scheduled in recent cycles - the 2026 edition ran May 9, 2026, which has already passed as of this listing's verification, so the May 8, 2027 date and May 6, 2027 deadline shown here are estimated based on the prior year's pattern, not yet officially announced. General market/browsing admission is inferred free (winery tasting fees are separate and not an entry charge, but this isn't explicitly confirmed) - left as null pending confirmation. Attendance is unconfirmed - 500 is a rough estimate for a small single-venue winery market.

name: South Padre Island Market Days Show

Described by an independent local news source as "the largest indoor market in South Texas," drawing both local and out-of-state vendors. Entry is curated - prospective vendors email contact info plus photos of their merchandise for review, not an open first-come booth rental. UNVERIFIED: exact booth fee is not published anywhere online (organizers only take email inquiries) - the $150 shown is an estimate based on comparable multi-day indoor Texas vendor shows, not a confirmed price; email spimarketdays@gmail.com or call (956) 345-5022 to confirm. Public admission is confirmed at $2 (an older article cites $1, suggesting the price has since risen). Attendance is unconfirmed - 8,000 is a rough estimate for a show billed as the region's largest indoor market across a 3-day run.

name: Peddler's Jingle Mingle Marketplace
